title: The LCP array written with -m 3 holds values greater than 3
body: Building `data/inputs/long_dna_sequence.fa` with `-m 3 --write-lcp` writes an LCP array that holds values of 4 and 5. With a max query length of 3 no LCP should exceed 3. The suffix order is unaffected. Found while sweeping the builder during sufr-caa3f2; present before and after that change.
close_reason: Fixed in a9bb934: find_lcp compares max_query_len - skip bytes past skip. Checked on long_dna -m 3 by recomputing every adjacent LCP from the suffix text. The tie order under -m moved too; see the note above. The N-run shortcut's copy of the defect is sufr-6ee7f5.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4be42394
notes.text: Reproduced at cff9fb6. `create --dna -m 3 --write-lcp data/inputs/long_dna_sequence.fa` followed by `list -p` shows 20001 LCP values. Of these, 3 are 4 and 10 are 5. The rest are 50 at 2 and 19919 at 3.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Jack decided on 2026-11-03 to fix this before sufr-a88738, the construction oracle, rather than have the oracle skip LCP under -m. The cause is the TODO in find_lcp (libsufr/src/build/sort.rs): len is set to max_query_len rather than max_query_len minus skip, and the N-run shortcut above it is not capped either. Priority raised to P2 for that.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Split on 2026-11-03: this issue is the len line only, fixed by max_query_len - skip. The N-run shortcut three lines above has the same defect and is sufr-6ee7f5, which batch 1 (sufr-a88738) also waits on. Found while checking the fix: the suffix order inside groups of equal keys also moves under -m, 149 of 20,001 rows on long_dna -m 3, because merge carried the uncapped LCP into its next decision. The issue's claim that the order was unaffected was wrong.

notes.author: Jeb Rosen/f3787cc2
notes.text: On dev this fix landed in 9984777 (PR #14), in `find_lcp` in `libsufr/src/sufr_builder.rs`, with two cases with a skip added to its test. a9bb934 is on `refactor` and not in dev's history.
